title: He/Ar mixtures in two piston cylinders: the mass ratio m1/m2 that makes P1 = 5 P2 at equal volume and temperature
summary: Two piston cylinders hold He and Ar with the same two masses swapped between the gases. Press start and the lab does the rest: every mass becomes molecules (a gram of He is ten times as many as a gram of Ar), PV = nRT turns equal volume and temperature into P1/P2 = n1/n2, a live bisection scans the mass ratio until the first piston needs five times the pressure, the pistons lock level, the result is checked by putting it back and by doubling the temperature, and two common wrong answers are audited before the answer is revealed. No prediction stage - input, run, watch, result.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: States of Matter: Gases and Liquids
topic: Ideal gas equation - pressure, moles and gas mixtures at equal volume and temperature
subtopics: Moles from mass and molar mass
Total moles of a gas mixture (Dalton's law)
Pressure proportional to moles at fixed V and T
Setting up and solving a ratio equation
concepts: n = m/M: with M(Ar) = 10 M(He), a mass of He contains ten times as many moles as the same mass of Ar
Cylinder 1: n1 = m1/M + m2/10M = (10m1 + m2)/10M; cylinder 2: n2 = (10m2 + m1)/10M
At equal V and T, PV = nRT gives P1/P2 = n1/n2 - R, T and V cancel
General form: m1/m2 = (pk - 1)/(k - p), which exists only when 1/k < p < k

methods: Solved independently before any key was consulted: n1 = 5 n2 gives 5m1 = 49m2, m1/m2 = 9.80
sympy: exact solution 49/5 with symbolic masses and molar mass; the general form (pk - 1)/(k - p); M cancels
An independent bisection on P1/P2(r) - 5 converges to 9.8000; P1/P2 rises monotonically so the root is unique
An ideal-gas calculation with real units (M = 4 and 40 g/mol, two sample masses, 250, 300 and 600 K) gives P1/P2 = 5 every time
Robustness and custom values: real molar masses give 9.82; p = 2 gives 2.38; p = k or k = p has no solution
Traps audited: m1/m2 = 5 gives P1/P2 = 3.4; m1/m2 = 0.10 gives 0.2; equating masses instead of moles has no solution
Independent script tests/verify_p1q09.py: 20 of 20 checks pass
Solution websites: MathonGo's published solution (their Q41) gives 9.8
The page computes the answer at run time with its own bisection and checks it against the exact formula; no answer value is written into the script

Headless-browser suite tests/sim_p1q09.js drives the whole page: the physics and its custom branches, the optional values and their warnings, the automatic nine-stage run from one START, the answer-panel messages, the live scan, the lock, the back-check and the temperature test, the audit and badges, the two charts, the reveal and its blink, the pressure explorer, replay, pause, reset, real-molar-mass and impossible custom runs, classroom mode, 390 and 360 px, reduced motion, the feed entries, and the real app shell opening it
Answer cross-checked afterwards against the official final key printed with the Paper 1 PDF: Q9 -> 9.80
verification.note: Built with the prayogx-next-question skill. Temperature is not given in the question; the page uses 300 K for the gauges and shows that it cancels. Moles are displayed in units of m2/(10 M_He).
